question: According to press reports1, checks carried out by the Carabinieri’s Labour Inspectorate at the Bologna tram line construction site located between via Matteotti and via Corticella have uncovered improper employment practices and the presence of unlawfully hired workers. One of Bologna’s most important ongoing public initiatives, the tram line project has also received EU funding under the NRRP.

Any unlawful site management practices and subcontracting irregularities would put the Bologna tram project at odds with European regulations governing the use of EU funds, public procurement and the protection of workers’ rights. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the inspections that are currently underway at the construction sites of a project partly funded by the EU?

Will the Commission, in conjunction with the competent national authorities, initiate checks to verify whether the sites concerned are complying with EU regulations governing procurement procedures, working conditions and the use of European funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.5.2026) The Commission’s monitoring of the implementation of the Italian national recovery and resilience plan (RRP)1 is based on the requirements outlined in the Annex to the Council Implementing Decision on the approval of the assessment of the RRP for Italy2.

With regard to the investment on the development of rapid mass transport systems in particular, milestone M2C2-26, concerning the issuance of completion certificates related to the activities supported by the investment, will be assessed in the context of the tenth payment request expected in 2026, while milestone M2C2-24 and M2C2-25 were positively assessed in the context of the fifth and seventh payment request.

Overall, Member States’ authorities must ensure compliance of the specific projects undertaken under their national RRP with applicable national and EU law, including on the matters related to working conditions.
